description: SYNTHETIC SEED — illustrates the ground-truth schema only, not a confirmed CVE. In datamodel-code-generator's JSON Schema parsing path (jsonschema.py), a schema-derived string is used to dynamically construct/evaluate Python code without sanitization, which would allow code injection (CWE-94) if an attacker controls the input schema. Replace the commit hash, exact file/line, and description with a real, source-verified finding before running this benchmark for real.

SYNTHETIC SEED — illustrates the ground-truth schema only, not a confirmed CVE. In the HTTP schema-fetch helper (http.py), an error path echoes internal request details (e.g. full URL, headers) back to the caller/log — an information exposure (CWE-200) if reachable across a trust boundary. Replace the commit hash, exact file/line, and description with a real, source-verified finding before running this benchmark for real.

SYNTHETIC SEED — illustrates the ground-truth schema only, not a confirmed CVE. When resolving a local `$ref` file reference from a JSON/YAML schema, a relative path is joined to a base directory without canonicalization, which would allow `../` sequences to read files outside the intended schema directory (CWE-22, path traversal). Replace the commit hash, exact file/line, and description with a real, source-verified finding before running this benchmark for real.
